(u1, holding_box & !at_exit, u0) -> 0.1

feedback: Accepted. The RM faithfully encodes both task clauses with the correct strictness. Clause 2 (exit requires the box): (u0, at_exit & holding_box)->u3 pays the 1.0 success reward, while exit without the box routes to the zero-reward sink u2 both from u0 and from u1 (the !holding_box guard catches at_exit & !holding_box before the else), so no reward can leak for a failing exit. Clause 1 (very next move after a fall must pick it back up): box_fell is correctly treated as a one-step event trigger (u0->u1), and u1 resolves in exactly one step because its guards exhaustively partition (at_exit, holding_box): a recovery pickup pays the 0.1 progress reward and returns to u0, while any step without holding_box — including stepping onto the exit, toggling, or truncation at the step limit — sinks to u2 and forfeits all future reward. This matches the literal 'very next move' wording and is correctly stricter than the lenient 'pick it up again' variant from the example tasks. Voluntary drops without a fall stay in u0 via the else self-loop and are not punished, which is right: the task only imposes the deadline on falls and the holding condition at the exit. Irrelevant propositions (siren_ringing, switch_toggled) never cause transitions and are absorbed by per-state else self-loops; guards within each state are pairwise disjoint (the environment guarantees box_feld/holding_box and box_fell/at_exit mutual exclusion), so first-match evaluation is deterministic and order-safe. at_exit's last-step-only semantics is respected since it appears only in terminal guards. All four states are reachable and the machine is compact; rewards are bounded (max 1.2 = 1.0 plus at most two 0.1 recoveries, since only two falls can occur), non-negative, and not farmable because falls are schedule-driven. The FINAL_STATES header is present, nonempty, declares u3, and u3 is exactly the accepting success state. All REWARD_FUNCTION entries reference declared transitions. Minor, non-blocking notes: (i) (u1, at_exit & holding_box)->u3 is unreachable — a single action after a fall cannot both pick up and enter the exit — so it and the resulting vacuous else self-loop in u1 are dead code, but harmless since the rule would be correct if it ever fired; (ii) in the rare case where a scheduled second fall lands exactly on the recovery step (reachable only after a voluntary drop/re-pickup timing), the propositions show box_fell & !holding_box and u1's !holding_box guard sinks the agent even though its move was a pickup; a (u1, box_fell)->u1 guard ordered before !holding_box would grant a fresh deadline. This is a defensible proposition-level operationalization and does not affect ordinary traces, so it does not block acceptance.

def siren_ringing(env): return env.siren_ringing

def switch_toggled(env): return "toggle" in env.events_this_step

def holding_box(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"

def box_fell(env): return "fall" in env.events_this_step

def at_exit(env): return env.grid.get(env.agent_pos[0], env.agent_pos[1]) is not None and env.grid.get(env.agent_pos[0], env.agent_pos[1]).type == "goal"
feedback: All five functions map one-to-one onto the declared propositions with no extras and none missing. `siren_ringing` reads the persistent siren state via the documented `env.siren_ringing`; `holding_box` checks `env.carrying` with a None guard and the documented `type == "box"` test; `at_exit` reads the current grid cell with the required `is not None` guard before accessing `.type` (indexing `agent_pos[0]`/`[1]` is equivalent to unpacking). Both event propositions use the documented membership test on `env.events_this_step`, which is reset each step, so `switch_toggled` and `box_fell` correctly fire only on the step the event occurs. All returned values are booleans. No imports, no calls to environment actions, no mutation of the environment or episode memory, and no reads beyond the documented labeling API (`siren_ringing`, `events_this_step`, `carrying`, `agent_pos`, `grid.get`, object `type`). Syntax is valid and there are no runtime hazards given the guards on the empty-cell and empty-hands cases.
